text:
Maya R.: Quick heads-up: after this morning's v2 soft-rollout a few tenants saw mismatched numbers in the console vs raw billing. Looks like attribution fields diverged in the pipeline.

Jake H.: Confirmed. Routing picks compat=v1 for some clients, model-selection later marks model=v2. ETL ends up grouping by both keys.

Leo T.: Can we pick one canonical source of truth at decision time? I'd prefer a header set by routing (X-Redwood-Attribution) that downstream systems must respect.

Priya V.: UX ask: until we canonicalize, hide the "estimated billing delta" in the rollforward preview and surface a warning banner: "Attribution mismatch detected - preview may be inaccurate."

Maya R.: Short-term mitigation: (1) route layer sets X-Redwood-Attribution; (2) ETL prefers that header; (3) console switches preview to sample-only. Owners: Maya (routing), Jake (ETL), Priya (console).

Jake H.: Implementation note: ETL will attribute missing header cases to v1 by default to avoid surprising customers. We'll run a 1% validation backfill after deploy.

Leo T.: Also add an enrichment guard so model-selector doesn't override the header. If header exists, enrichment should add model_variant but not change attribution.

ops-bot: Scheduled 1% backfill window 02:00-02:30 UTC. Will page oncall if CPU > 70% or latency > 200ms.

Priya V.: I'll update console copy and mock a preview card showing "Attribution sample: canonicalized / mismatch" plus 3 sample trace ids.

Maya R.: Thanks team. I'll open routing PR now and tag Jake and Leo for quick review. We'll hold further rollforwards until validation is green.
